step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.premiseCheck: The dispatch asserts 'the EXISTING acquisition pipeline... we already have machinery for.' Verified this claim directly rather than assuming it.
step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.hauskaFactoryGrepResult: grep -rn 'txgio' src/cli.mjs: zero hits. No CLI verb named txgio/acquire/refresh exists. landing-import.mjs's SOURCES map reads FROM txgio_parcel (already-loaded) and writes TO landing_txgio_parcel -- it refreshes a DERIVED landing table from whatever is CURRENTLY in txgio_parcel; it does not fetch anything new from the public TxGIO/StratMap service. Six 'factory-landing-*' Cloud Run job resources (landing-parcel, landing-pipeline, landing-cad, landing-footprint, landing-wells, landing-import) all run the identical landing-import verb with different --source args -- none of them reach the public source.
step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.caldwellGeomCloseCorroboration: _inbox/2026-09-02_parcel-caldwell-geom_close.json's own independent investigation reached the identical conclusion from a different angle: 'txgio_parcel is an external table with no migration, trigger, or job code in hauska-factory referencing its geom column at all' -- the raw acquisition is confirmed external to this repo by a second, independent card.
step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.actualMechanismLocated: OPS-1_texas_source_registry.md names the real path: TxGIO StratMap bulk zips, one per FIPS, at a public URL (data.geographic.texas.gov), no auth, browser User-Agent required; 'Hauska ingest subset in legacy-design-tools/lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/parse.ts' -- a DIFFERENT repo than this card is scoped into (card.json names repo: hauska-factory).
step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.recentRealUseOfThatMechanism_P78: Found and read the actual most recent invocation: P-78 (2026-08-25, _inbox/2026-08-25_p78_announce_bastrop_48021.md and 32+ sibling county announces), which DID perform a real network fetch of a StratMap zip and wrote into cad_property via CORTEX_DATABASE_URL using an 'adapter:stratmap' tier. Read closely, P-78 was NOT a vintage refresh: its own announce doc states 'Source: TxGIO StratMap 202503 zip' -- the SAME already-stale March 2025 vintage already loaded, explicitly scoped as a 'leftover' fill (filling null year_built/land_acres on EXISTING 2025-tax-year rows plus 726 same-vintage inserts), with an explicit scope lock 'No L17 flip' (the vintage tier itself was never advanced). Live-confirmed: cad_property now carries a 'stratmap-roll' tier for 5 of 6 counties (all but 48309/McLennan) ingested 2026-08-25, but this coexists with the same 202503/202507/202508 txgio_parcel vintages already measured above -- P-78 changed CAD attribute presentation, not the underlying geometry vintage. The containment-total cross-check above (still exactly 981,405) independently confirms P-78 did not touch containment.
step2Investigation_reAcquisitionMechanis.conclusion: The dispatch's step-2 premise does not hold as stated. There is no re-acquisition pipeline inside hauska-factory. The real mechanism (a real, working, network-fetching StratMap adapter) exists in legacy-design-tools, a repo this card is not scoped into, and its one recent real invocation (P-78) was a narrow leftover-field fill using the ALREADY-STALE vintage, not a genuine refresh to a newer StratMap drop. Building or invoking a genuine statewide re-acquisition myself would mean either (a) writing new integration code reaching a live external government data source across six large counties (Travis alone is 894,657 raw parcel rows) -- squarely the 'new pipeline' the dispatch explicitly forbids -- or (b) working inside legacy-design-tools without this card's scope covering that repo. Neither is something to improvise without operator/planner routing.
